articleTitle: Liver Mass With Central or Eccentric Scar

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial arterial-phase CECT shows a homogeneously and brightly enhancing mass with a central scar . The mass became isodense with liver on portal venous phase.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial 20-minute delayed T1 MR shows a large mass that retains contrast more than underlying liver. The central scar does not take up or retain gadoxetate.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR shows a brightly and homogeneously enhancing mass with a central scar ; this is classic FNH.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large mass with peripheral nodular enhancement isodense to vessels. A central scar , with a small focus of calcification, did not fill in on delayed imaging. These are typical features of giant hemangiomas.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR shows a large, hyperintense mass with a central scar that is very bright, typical of a large hemangioma with progressive nodular enhancement on arterial , venous , and delayed phases.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 MR shows a large mass that is very bright and well defined. A central scar is even more intense, typical of large cavernous hemangioma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial arterial-phase CECT in an older woman shows a large, heterogeneous, hypervascular mass with foci of necrosis, giving it a mottled or mosaic appearance. The age of the patient and absence of calcification favored conventional hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), as opposed to fibrolamellar HCC, confirmed on biopsy.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large mass with an eccentric scar or necrotic area. Tumor invasion of portal vein helps to identify this as HCC.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows a heterogeneous mass in the left lobe. At resection, the focus of high attenuation was hemorrhage, and the lower density foci were necrosis and fibrosis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial venous-phase T1 C+ MR shows a large, enhancing mass with a central nonenhancing scar .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT in this older patient with colon cancer shows shows multiple lesions with faint central calcification .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial portal venous-phase CECT in this older patient with colon cancer shows multiple metastases with central, low-density necrosis or fibrosis. The faint calcification is more difficult to recognize on contrast-enhanced imaging.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 22-year-old man shows a heterogeneous, hypervascular mass with a large, calcified central scar . Note the similar enhancement of tumor in a cardiophrenic node .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in a young woman with a large, heterogeneously enhancing left hepatic lobe fibrolamellar HCC shows a central necrotic scar .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large mass that fills the left lobe with low density and calcified portions of the scar.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large hepatic mass with foci of scar or necrosis . Capsular retraction and occlusion of the portal vein and bile duct help confirm cholangiocarcinoma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ FS MR shows a large, hypointense mass with progressive enhancement on arterial , portal venous , and delayed phases due to fibrotic changes and a nonenhancing central scar .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-17

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a young woman shows multiple peripheral hypovascular lesions with a target appearance. The subcapsular lesions are associated with retraction of the overlying liver capsule .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2 FS MR in a young woman shows multiple peripheral and confluent masses , many with hyperintense central necrosis or scar . These are typical features of hepatic epithelial hemangioendothelioma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial arterial-phase T1 C+ MR in a hypercoagulable patient shows multiple hypervascular foci . Some of the lesions seem to have a hypointense rim, while others have a hypointense central scar .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ MR in a hypercoagulable patient 2 hours after IV administration of gadobenate dimeglumine shows persistent uptake and retention of the agent within the nodules , indicating functional hepatocytes and deficient biliary ducts within the lesions.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1 C+ MR in a patient with Budd-Chiari syndrome shows multiple hypervascular nodules , some of which have a central scar . These multiple large, regenerative nodules (nodular regenerative hyperplasia) confirmed transplantation.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient with Budd-Chiari syndrome and nodular regenerative hyperplasia shows a central scar and doughnut-like enhancement. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is also seen .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: In this patient with Budd-Chiari syndrome and multiple hypervascular nodules, trichrome stain shows green staining of the central scar and the capsule of the nodule, typical features of the macroscopic form of nodular regenerative hyperplasia or large regenerative nodules.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-24

downloadSentinel:
Completed the full autonomous build for Liver Mass With Central or Eccentric Scar.

Core Validation Pathway A passed using the uploaded Core Radiology, Second Edition, Gastrointestinal Imaging → Liver. Relevant coverage spans approximately GI 105–122, with the central-scar pattern explicitly summarized on GI 119: FNH, fibrolamellar HCC, and giant hemangioma. The surrounding Core sections provide the additional HCC, adenoma, metastasis, cholangiocarcinoma, epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, and Budd-Chiari/regenerative-nodule discriminators used in the synthesis.

The final deck contains 40 cards / 40 TSV lines: 9 Primary UNKNOWNs covering all 9 atomic STATdx teaching clusters and all 24 selected primary images, 6 Mechanism cards, 5 Boards Trap cards, 4 Epidemiology High-Yield cards, and 16 other High-Yield cards. Differential Drill and Definition sections were correctly omitted because they were not explicitly requested. The 22-column audit, unique Clinical_Context-code audit, trigger-isolation audit, blank Tags-column audit, summary-identity audit, Section A cardinality audit, and supplied-caption verbatim audit all passed.

The supplied STATdx URLs could not be authenticated/downloaded from this runtime, so I did not falsely claim that the image binaries were retrieved. The TSV instead preserves the exact source-qualified SDX-##_STATdx_plain_...jpg / SDX-##_STATdx_annotated_...jpg references and the supplied captions.
